# Gaps per reef (what is unknown, assumed or weak) - generated by src/build_reefs.py + manual notes in src/gaps_manual.py

## narrowneck-gold-coast - Narrowneck Reef (Gold Coast Reef), Gold Coast, Queensland
Status counts: {'sourced': 17, 'derived': 19, 'assumed': 0, 'unknown': 3}
- UNKNOWN fields: swell_tp_s, arm_angle_to_swell_deg, surfable_days_per_year
  - swell_tp_s: no Tp for the Narrowneck design/typical surf found in the repo; Blacka 2013 A.2 p.100: actual Gold Coast waves are shorter period than the modelled long-period clean swell (value not stated).
  - arm_angle_to_swell_deg: not computed: dominant SE swell direction is given only qualitatively; with shore-normal bearing 86.2 deg true and a SE swell (~135 deg) the swell arrives about 49 deg off shore-normal before refraction (ASSUMPTION of 135 deg).
  - surfable_days_per_year: not stated for Narrowneck; EcoShape (card R6) says the reef broke waves about 50 % of the time (basis unknown).
- ASSUMED fields: none
- Crest datum: MSQ gives AHD = LAT + 0.760 m, the papers (Jackson 2007, Corbett 2023) imply AHD = LAT + 1.00 m: crest is 1.44 or 1.20 m below LAT (0.24 m; ask the City / MSQ). The model uses MSQ.
- Footprint 6,239 m2 is a LOWER BOUND (deeper toe not visible on the 2020 photo); bed under the reef is read from a colour figure (Corbett 2023 Fig 3, +-0.4 m, placed +-10 m); nearshore bed (0-190 m) assumed. Toe depth 6.1 m (model edge, -6 m contour) vs about 7.1 m at the design toe.
- Surfable swell: only Hs ~1.0 m (NSW review, basis unstated) and "SE, long-period clean swell". Needs Black & Mead (2001, J. Coastal Research 115-130) and Jackson et al. 2007 for design Hs/Tp/direction (not obtained).
- Original-design (1999) crest was -1.0 m AHD, built -1.5 m AHD, later topped/settled; the 2018 crest -2.2 m AHD is one level for the whole reef; settlement 1-2 m locally.
- Sediment outcome is contested (20-50 m salient vs misreading, NSW review); Vieira da Silva et al. 2021 (offshore bars) was used only via the 3D notes.

## cables-reef-wa - Cables Reef (Cable Station reef), Perth / Fremantle, Western Australia
Status counts: {'sourced': 20, 'derived': 14, 'assumed': 1, 'unknown': 3}
- UNKNOWN fields: reef_height_m, tide_spring_range_m, swell_tp_s
  - reef_height_m: Blacka 2013 A.1: reef to 6 m depth; no height statement. Model: rock surface on measured bed; see depth_gap_m.
  - tide_spring_range_m: spring range not stated in the sources read; BoM Fremantle recorded extremes 1.947 m and -0.100 m above gauge zero (1987-2011), i.e. a 2.05 m extreme range (METHODS_3D s3.2), not a spring range. Tide is mixed, mainly diurnal.
  - swell_tp_s: not found in the repo for Cables (Pattiaratchi 1999 report not read for this field).
- ASSUMED fields: crest_depth_lat_m
  - crest_depth_lat_m: derived: surveyed crest -1.55 m AHD; LWD = -0.716 m AHD (Roelse et al. 1975 Table 3; METHODS_3D s3.1) -> 0.83 m below LWD ASSUMPTION: Fremantle low-water datum (LWD) is used in place of LAT; LAT/HAT for Fremantle were not found on the pages read (METHODS_3D s3.6). Pitt 2009 says crest ~1.5 m below the lowest tide (original not seen).
- Design RL datum ambiguity (reading A RL = Fremantle LWD, B RL = MSL: 0.716 m); the surveyed crest (-1.55 m AHD) avoids it; LAT/HAT for Fremantle not found, LWD used as LAT proxy (ASSUMED).
- Tide: only "range 0.8 m"; spring and mean ranges not separated. Design swell (0.5-3.5 m, 45 deg peel) is from secondary pages; Pattiaratchi (1999) report (mirror http://joas.free.fr/studies/bei/g2s/reefdesign.pdf) should give design Hs, Tp, direction: not read for this dataset.
- Year: 1998 (Mead & Borrero 2011) vs 1999 (WA Government media statement, card); volume 3,500 / 4,671 (survey) / 5,000 / 5,500 m3; material granite vs limestone; surveyed surface at the outline edge stands up to 2.65 m above the bed (survey interpolated between lines).

## prattes-reef-el-segundo - Pratte's Reef (permit name Chevron Reef), El Segundo / Dockweiler Beach, California
Status counts: {'sourced': 15, 'derived': 18, 'assumed': 2, 'unknown': 3}
- UNKNOWN fields: swell_hs_m, swell_tp_s, surfable_days_per_year
  - swell_hs_m: no wave-height statement for Pratte's found in the repo sources; Santa Monica Bay is a low-energy, W-SW swell site. Surfline comment: reef broke only on a few large swells (card R7).
  - swell_tp_s: not found in the repo.
  - surfable_days_per_year: none stated; no consistently surfable wave.
- ASSUMED fields: seaward_ramp_length_m, mean_seaward_slope
  - seaward_ramp_length_m: ASSUMED bag-stack side slope 1 H : 1 V (range 0.5-2.5 H per 1 V), so ramp = gap x 1.0 (0.7-3.4 m) No section of the Phase I reef exists; the face of a 1.2 m bag course is the only "ramp".
  - mean_seaward_slope: ASSUMED 1:1 (range 1:0.5 to 1:2.5)
- No as-built plan: the footprint is the Skelly design drawing; stack height not stated; model volume 443 m3 vs 695-782 m3 (80-90 % fill) vs 869 m3 nominal vs 1,350 m3 (Mead & Borrero, all phases).
- Ramp and slope are ASSUMED (bag side slope 1:1, range 0.5-2.5): treat as order of magnitude only. Crest (apex 2.68 m below MSL) is one point stated by the monitors (-6 ft MLLW).
- Offshore distance: 103 m (model, MSL waterline) vs 50 m (NSW review, undisturbed shoreline). Swell climate for Santa Monica Bay not in the repo. Tide is mixed semidiurnal; "spring range" given as the great diurnal range MHHW-MLLW.

## mount-maunganui-reef - Mount Maunganui Reef (Mount Reef), Mount Maunganui main beach, Bay of Plenty
Status counts: {'sourced': 16, 'derived': 16, 'assumed': 3, 'unknown': 3}
- UNKNOWN fields: swell_dir, arm_angle_to_swell_deg, surfable_days_per_year
  - swell_dir: swell direction not confirmed in the sources read (open ocean beach, Bay of Plenty).
  - arm_angle_to_swell_deg: swell direction not confirmed.
  - surfable_days_per_year: not stated; "three or four times" since completion (local surfer, ~2010).
- ASSUMED fields: reef_height_m, seabed_depth_toe_m, seabed_depth_at_crest_m
  - reef_height_m: METHODS_3D KN "Reef height above the bed": maximum 2.85 m default version; Moores 2006 largest bags 3.5 m high x 50 m long
  - seabed_depth_toe_m: ASSUMED as-built bed at the reef centre -3.6 m CD (= 4.73 m below MSL), Lior decision D1 2026-10-07; chosen to reproduce the stated 2,800 m3 No source states the 2008-09 bed. Evidence range: Oct 2006 survey beside the unfinished reef 2.0-3.7 m (CD assumed); BoPRC p23 3.0-4.0 m in 2008; ASR Installed ring -4.46 m CD; consent depth 3.7-4.6 m; 2013 survey -2.4 to -3.3 m CD; Navionics 2026 -2.76 m CD. Alternative "later seabed" -2.8 m CD = 3.93 m below MSL; Blacka depth 3.0-4.5 m. Bed slope 1:64 (Navionics 3-5 m).
  - seabed_depth_at_crest_m: same assumed bed (alongshore-uniform profile; the bed varies by < 0.1 m across the 5 m between toe and crest)
- Toe depth is an ASSUMPTION (as-built bed -3.6 m CD = 4.73 m below MSL, Lior decision D1): evidence runs from 2.4 to 4.5 m CD; the 2013 multibeam DEM (reef deflated, partly buried) shows bed 3.9-4.3 m below MSL and the highest cell 1.29 m below MSL.
- Ramp (5.1 m) and slope (0.53) are a hand calculation from the METHODS rules (1:1 skirt + DEM-shaped rise), not a grid extraction; DEM flanks are near vertical over the last 0.5-1 m.
- Swell direction and design wave not recorded; volume 2,800 built vs 6,500 designed; reef built ~50 m closer to shore than designed; removed 2014, so durability is a closed record.
- Cost price year (2008) assumed.

## boscombe-surf-reef - Boscombe Surf Reef, Boscombe, Bournemouth, Dorset (Poole Bay)
Status counts: {'sourced': 19, 'derived': 19, 'assumed': 0, 'unknown': 0}
- UNKNOWN fields: none
- ASSUMED fields: none
- Datum of the April 2011 survey plot is ASSUMED to be chart datum (Bournemouth CD = ODN - 1.40 m, ODN ~ MSL): all absolute depths shift by 1.4 m if it is ODN; relief does not. Crest +0.5 m ACD = 0.90 m below MSL.
- Seaward flank 1:3 (+-30 %) is an assumption of the idealised loft (survey flanks 1:1.5 to 1:7); ramp 14 m and slope 0.33 depend on it. The reef is shown as built in 2009; the 2011 survey shows container failure.
- Surf performance: Davidson (2010) 4 of 11 objectives met (via Wikipedia) vs designers 7 of 9; no measured surfable days; typical Hs 0.5 m / T 4 s from the NSW review; design swell direction 191 deg.

- Crest is ABOVE MSL (+0.19 m; negative depth): the surf reef dries at low and mid tide in a macro-tidal (spring 4.3 m) setting. MSL = +0.31 mODN +-0.15 m is a 4-level mean.
- No wave-climate or surfing measurement (Borrero & Mead 2010 surfing assessment and HR Wallingford physical-model report not obtained); surf outcome "unknown".
- Seabed under the rock follows a design bed level (about -4.0 mODN) and a hand-read contour figure; ramp/slope are medians over a long diagonal mound (axis 64 deg to the shore) and are not a meaningful peel-ramp measure. Offshore distance is from the defence line (back of the shingle beach), not MSL.
- Cost GBP 13 M is for the whole Phase 1 coastal-defence works, not the reef alone.
